a0.instructions: Read the order. Is the whole army (Prussian Army (General Frederick II); also called the army, the King's army, the headquarters, my headquarters, the King, the Feldmarschall) told to do something as one body, for example 'everything forward' or 'the army will retire'? An instruction to particular generals or formations alone does not count.

criteria.true: yes, an instruction to the whole army at once
criteria.false: no, only particular formations are instructed, or none

a1.instructions: Read the order. Does it give Heavy artillery (artillery, General Prussian artillery commander (unrecorded)); also called the artillery, the heavy guns, the batteries, the Prussian guns an instruction: is this formation or its general named, addressed as 'you', or clearly meant (by arm, e.g. 'the cavalry', 'the artillery', 'the hussars') as one who must do or not do something? Being mentioned only as a place to follow, wait for, or stay behind does not count, and neither does being the 'you' of a condition such as 'once you are engaged'.

criteria.true: yes, this formation is given an instruction
criteria.false: no, it is not instructed (perhaps only mentioned)

c0_prohib.instructions: Read this part of the order: «Katte, keep Zieten's hussars on Hülsen's left flank while he attacks Křečhoř.». Is it a prohibition or a limit, telling someone what not to do or how far not to go ('do not charge the line without my order', 'not to be drawn beyond X', 'attack nothing', 'only on my express order'), rather than an instruction to do something?

criteria.true: yes, it forbids or limits something
criteria.false: no, it is an instruction to act, or information

c0_forbid.instructions: Read this part of the order: «Katte, keep Zieten's hussars on Hülsen's left flank while he attacks Křečhoř.». If it forbids or limits something, what is forbidden?

criteria.none: nothing in particular is forbidden, or it is not a prohibition
criteria.charge_formed_infantry: not to charge the enemy's formed infantry: his line, his battalions, his squares, the troops on the heights
criteria.attack: not to attack or assault at all, or only on a further order ('attack nothing', 'come into the attack only on my order')
criteria.pursue: not to pursue or follow up a beaten or fleeing enemy
criteria.advance_beyond: not to go beyond or farther than a certain place, not to be drawn off
criteria.engage: not to engage, fight, halt or turn against the enemy, or be drawn into a fight

c0_trig.instructions: Read this part of the order: «Katte, keep Zieten's hussars on Hülsen's left flank while he attacks Křečhoř.». Does it tie what it orders to an event or a time?

criteria.none: no event or time is named: it is to be done at once, or it is a standing rule
criteria.start: it is to be done only when or after something happens or a time comes ('as soon as', 'once', 'when', 'after', 'at <time>')
criteria.until: it is to last only until something happens or a time comes ('until', 'till')

c0_event.instructions: Read this part of the order: «Katte, keep Zieten's hussars on Hülsen's left flank while he attacks Křečhoř.». If it names an event or a time on which what it orders starts or ends, what is that event?

criteria.reached: a formation reaches, takes, holds or passes a place
criteria.engaged: a formation is engaged with the enemy or attacks
criteria.seen: the enemy comes into sight or approaches
criteria.routs: some body breaks, flees or gives way
criteria.order: a further order from the commander arrives

c0_who.instructions: Read this part of the order: «Katte, keep Zieten's hussars on Hülsen's left flank while he attacks Křečhoř.». If it names such an event, whom does the event concern: which formation must reach or hold the place, be engaged, or break? 'You' is the general this part is given to; 'he' or 'him' is whoever the order last named.

criteria.self: the general or formation this part of the order is given to ('you', 'he', 'it')
criteria.w4: Flank-guard grenadiers (General Major von Kahlden (senior battalion commander, EST))
criteria.w5: Prince Franz's brigade (General Prince Franz of Brunswick)

c0_where.instructions: Read this part of the order: «Katte, keep Zieten's hussars on Hülsen's left flank while he attacks Křečhoř.». If the event is reaching, taking, holding or passing a place, which place?

criteria.f49_our_left_flank: our left flank (a place relative to our own army as it now stands)
criteria.f50_our_right_flank: our right flank (a place relative to our own army as it now stands)
criteria.f51_our_centre: our centre (a place relative to our own army as it now stands)
criteria.f52_our_rear: our rear (a place relative to our own army as it now stands)
